land.text: the western plain surrendered on 1 February 1662

successors.note: The Dutch held Keelung until 1668 (successor of that last holding not named on the pages; the Tungning dossier reads it as the kingdom, confidence 1).

capitals.name: Zeelandia (Fort Zeelandia, now Anping, Tainan)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Zeelandia (now Anping, Tainan)'; the first temporary fort 'was replaced four years later by the more substantial Fort Zeelandia'. The Dutch kept Keelung to 1668.

correction.text: Tayouan, Fort Zeelandia and Sakam (Fort Provintia) around Tainan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (the 'Dutch East India Company' row, dutch-east-india-company, does not carry Formosa in its ledger). Tayouan and the Sinkan lands: 'In 1625, they bought a piece of land from the Sinkanders and built the town of Sakam'. No area on the page.

correction.text: the west-coast plain south of 24 N, whose villages swore allegiance

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after 'the pacification campaigns of 1635-1636, more and more villages came to the Dutch to swear allegiance'; 'the extent of their control was limited to the plains on the west coast'. The ring (119.8-121.1 E, 21.8-24.0 N) cut to the island is a reading: the page gives no northern limit for 1636.

union.text: Keelung, the former Spanish San Salvador
Tamsui, the former Spanish Fort Santo Domingo

correction.text: Dutch Formosa after 1642: the west-coast plains with Keelung and Tamsui

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Dutch 'dislodge the small Spanish-Filipino contingent from their fortress and drive them from the island' in August 1642, adding Keelung and Tamsui to the west-coast plains. 'This territory was acquired from 1624 to 1642'. 'Isolated pockets on the east coast' are not placed by the page.

correction.text: Keelung, the Dutch fortress held until 1668

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after 1 February 1662 only Keelung remains ('The Dutch held out at Keelung until 1668 when they withdrew from Taiwan completely'). The Dutch Formosa page adds 'the Dutch retook the northern fortress at Keelung in 1664', which implies the Zheng had it in between; this dossier keeps it Dutch throughout.

region.text: Tayouan, where the Dutch retreated from the Pescadores

ledger.note: 1624: the Dutch settle on Formosa. 'Established: 1624'; after the Ming forced them out, the Dutch were 'withdrawing from the Pescadores to Formosa' (they 'were forced to sue for peace on 3 August'); a temporary fort at Tayouan was 'replaced four years later by the more substantial Fort Zeelandia'.

region.text: the west-coast plain south of 24 N: the villages that swore allegiance

ledger.note: 1636: the Dutch pacify the west-coast villages. 'Following the pacification campaigns of 1635-1636, more and more villages came to the Dutch to swear allegiance', 'most of the villages being required to swear allegiance to the Dutch and then largely being left to govern themselves'. The year is the page's; the northern limit is the researcher's reading.

August 1642: the Dutch return to Keelung. 'In August that year the Dutch returned to Keelung with four large ships' after the 1641 assault failed ('the positions were well-defended and the attacking troops were not able to breach the walls'); the Spanish governor in Manila had recalled most of the Formosa troops.
August 1642: 'After six days of battle, the small force surrendered the fort.' The page gives no day.

region.text: Spanish northern Formosa: Keelung and Tamsui

ledger.note: August 1642: the Dutch take northern Taiwan. The Dutch Formosa page: 'managing to dislodge the small Spanish-Filipino contingent from their fortress and drive them from the island'; 'This territory was acquired from 1624 to 1642'. The Spanish page names the fortress at Keelung only; Tamsui is the researcher's addition.

region.text: Tayouan, Fort Zeelandia and Fort Provintia

ledger.note: April 1661: Koxinga lands. 'The fleet arrived at Tayouan on 2 April'; 'On 4 April, Fort Provintia surrendered to Zheng forces'; 'On 7 April, Zheng's army besieged Fort Zeelandia'.

1 February 1662: the surrender terms are finalised; 'On the 9th of February, the remaining Dutch East India Company personnel left Taiwan' (the Dutch Formosa page says the Dutch surrendered on 12 January 1662).

region.text: the west-coast plains held by the Dutch, from Fort Zeelandia to Hsinchu

ledger.note: February 1662: the Dutch lose Taiwan's plains. The war 'ended the Dutch East India Company's rule over Taiwan'; the Dutch 'held out at Keelung until 1668'.

1668: the Dutch leave Taiwan. 'The Dutch held out at Keelung until 1668 when they withdrew from Taiwan completely.' The pages do not say who took Keelung (confidence 1: bridged to the Zheng); the infobox gives 'Disestablished: 1662', which is the loss of the plains.

wars.name: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
wars.outcome: Ming loyalists' victory: the Dutch East India Company lost Taiwan on 1 February 1662, except Keelung.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Spanish Formosa
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: after a failed assault in 1641 the Dutch returned to Keelung in August 1642 with four large ships and the Spanish fort surrendered after six days.
wars.note: The Spanish Formosa page; the Dutch Formosa page puts the whole 'territory acquired from 1624 to 1642'.

wars.name: Dutch campaign at Keelung against the Zheng
wars.outcome: The Dutch 'retook the northern fortress at Keelung in 1664' after skirmishes and 'held out at Keelung until 1668 when they withdrew from Taiwan completely'.
wars.note: The Tungning page gives only 'held out ... until 1668'.

certainty.note: The Dutch ruled villages that 'swore allegiance' and were 'largely left to govern themselves'; the interior and the east coast had no line, and the northern limit is a ring.

notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from four pages. A state Cliopatria lacks; it arose on stateless land (the Sinkan lands at Tayouan; the 1622-1624 Pescadores base at Makung is not drawable on the grid), so predecessors is empty; the VOC row (dutch-east-india-company, 1602-1799) carries no Formosa event in its ledger, so this colony's shapes are the only record of the Dutch on Taiwan. Type colony (a dependency ruled from Batavia); family 'france' follows the other Dutch colonies.

Not settled: (1) the infobox says Disestablished 1662 but the Dutch kept Keelung to 1668: the dossier ends in 1668; (2) the Dutch Formosa page says the Dutch 'retook the northern fortress at Keelung in 1664', which implies the Zheng held Keelung 1662-1664, while the Siege and Tungning pages say the Dutch 'held out at Keelung until 1668'; this dossier follows the second reading (a gap-filler should open 'Dutch-Zheng conflict'); (3) the northern limit of the west-coast plains (rings stand in) and the 'isolated pockets on the east coast' are not placed on the page; (4) the surrender date is 12 January 1662 on the Dutch Formosa and Tungning pages and 1 February 1662 on the Siege page (terms finalised 1 February); (5) the Pescadores base 1622-1624 and Liuqiu Island (1636 expedition) are not drawn; (6) the Penghu islands resolve to no cells on the grid. Gazetteer: 'Tamsui' is missing (a 15 km radius round 121.44 E, 25.17 N is used).
